summary: Preserve native stop, retry, abort and process-exit outcomes in conversation replay

replay.detail: No replay trigger or graph projection invalidation is added; native outcomes are normalized on read from the owner machine per request.

schema.detail: No SQLite migration or stored transcript class is introduced. Nothing about these outcomes is stored in the database; native transcripts remain owner-local source files.

rules.detail: No new claim kind, checkpoint rule or sealing coordination requirement is introduced; replay still does not authorize ask recovery or remote controls.

compatibility.detail: Native provider outcomes are now passed through in full: push_omp_stop carries the harness-recorded errorMessage, retryRecovery, errorStatus and errorId, and session-exit entries carry the complete exit record including pendingToolCalls arguments/intent and unknown fields. Only transport size and paging limits apply, visibly marked, with owner continuations recovering exact values. Recognized planned exits (normal/dispose/manual, sigterm/sigint/sighup, exit code zero) are status entries labelled stopped instead of errors or completed, so a deliberate stop is not mistaken for a failed or successful turn. Clients that switch on timeline status values see the new stopped vocabulary entry: TimelineStatus is an open vocabulary, current generated clients carry the value, and the frozen legacy Swift decoder predates it. Fatal and unknown exits remain non-retryable errors.

downtime.detail: No additional upgrade service stop or measured outage is introduced; normal member and client restarts apply.

manual.detail: No data repair, grant conversion or configuration change is needed.

recovery.detail: No additional recovery procedure is introduced. Outcomes are re-read from the owner machine's native transcript on each request; preserve native transcripts and follow existing roll-forward guidance.
